title: Three Nights and One Short Wand
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：magic　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 magic 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the magician ① performed the magic that no onlooker in the theatre would have recorded, and he said the performing was the whole of the night. The ② magic, meaning the trick itself and not the wand, ran three nights and stayed unrecorded in the book; a magic, he said, is the only thing in a theatre that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ magic in that theatre had the same short wand beside it, and the ④ magic at the far stage, meaning the secret they kept for the children to guess and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A magic, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the magician said the recording is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the magic was the whole of the matter, meaning the wonder and not the trick. The ⑥ magic, meaning the wonder and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; magic, he said, is either something you perform or the only word that means both a trick and a wonder. He said the wonder is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ magic had become a line in a poster, and the poster had become an argument about the short wand. The ⑧ magic of the whole thing, the magician wrote in August, was one theatre and three nights of recording; magic, he said, is either the secret at the far stage or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ magic I remember is the trick recorded in the poster, which closed in 1964 and is still recorded as the quietest in the theatre. A ⑩ magic, my mother said in 1966, is the only trick that improves by being recorded; every magic, she said, is a wonder that has agreed to look like a trick. She said the wonder was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 魔术；魔法（指戏院里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 魔术；魔法（指那场魔术本身，与魔杖相对）
C. 固定搭配：perform the magic 表演这一场魔术
D. n. 魔术；魔法（指留给孩子们猜的那一个那一场）
E. n. 戏法之事（抽象总称，指一处戏院的魔术之事）
F. n. 魔术；魔法（指戏报里写到、被记述的的那一场）
G. n. 惊奇、幻境（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 幻境（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: performed the magic that no onlooker in the theatre would have recorded
The magic, meaning the trick itself and not the wand
the magic at the far stage
the magic was the whole of the matter
the magic had become a line in a poster
The magic of the whole thing
A magic, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: perform the magic 意为“表演这一场魔术”，1957 年那位魔术师把戏院里没有一位看客肯记述的一场魔术做了一遍。
magic 意为“魔术；魔法”，指那场魔术本身而不是魔杖，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记述。
magic 意为“魔术；魔法”，指戏院里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一根短短的魔杖。
magic 意为“魔术；魔法”，指最远那处台口留给孩子们猜的那一个那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
magic 意为“惊奇、幻境”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份惊奇就是那件事的全部。
magic 意为“幻境”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那场魔术，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
magic 意为“魔术；魔法”，指戏报里写到、被记述的的那一场，到 1962 年这一场成了戏报里的一行。
magic 意为“戏法之事”，魔术师八月写道，整件事的魔术之事是一处戏院和三个夜晚的记述。
magic 意为“魔术；魔法”，我记得的是戏报里记述过的那一场，1964 年演完了，至今仍被说成戏院里最安静的一场。
magic 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，魔术是唯一会因为被好好记述而变得更好的魔术。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年那位魔术师表演了戏院里没有一位看客肯记述的一场魔术，他说这一遍才是那个夜晚的全部。（perform the magic）
那场魔术，指的是那场魔术本身而不是魔杖，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记述。（magic）
那处戏院里每一场魔术旁边都有同一根短短的魔杖。（magic）
最远那处台口那场魔术，指的是他们留给孩子们猜的那一个那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（magic）
叔叔说这份惊奇就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那场魔术。（magic）
1966 年母亲说，魔术是唯一会因为被好好记述而变得更好的魔术。（magic）
answers: In 1957 the magician performed the magic that no onlooker in the theatre would have recorded, and he said the performing was the whole of the night.
The magic, meaning the trick itself and not the wand, ran three nights and stayed unrecorded in the book.
Every magic in that theatre had the same short wand beside it.
The magic at the far stage, meaning the secret they kept for the children to guess and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the magic was the whole of the matter, meaning the wonder and not the trick.
A magic, my mother said in 1966, is the only trick that improves by being recorded.
